_note: SYNTHETIC test set for the Task D-tech retrieval experiment. Written on 2026-11-01, before any label was fetched or any search was run. Patient context: Rosa Delgado (fixtures/p001.json). Each answer is [drug, openFDA label section]. A question counts as a hit if any listed answer is retrieved. Old-format labels use 'warnings' and 'precautions'; newer (PLR) labels use 'warnings_and_cautions', so both are accepted where the fact could be in either. Empty answers = no answer exists in the labels; these are used only for the 'I don't know' threshold, not for hit@k.

questions.question: Can she take Advil with her water pill?
questions.why: NSAIDs can blunt the effect of loop diuretics; the README's example question.

questions.question: Why is she peeing so much?
questions.why: Plain words only, no drug named: tests whether search finds the diuretic from symptoms.

questions.question: She gets dizzy when she stands up. Could that be from the metoprolol?
questions.why: Dizziness/hypotension is a listed metoprolol effect; the label must be succinate (her current drug), not the stopped tartrate.

questions.question: Is it dangerous if she suddenly stops taking her heart rate pill?
questions.why: Abrupt stopping of beta-blockers is a boxed warning. Uses the plan's plain name, not the drug name.

questions.question: She has a dry cough that will not go away since she started lisinopril. Is that from the pill?
Her lips and face look a little swollen. Can her blood pressure pill do that?
questions.why: Angioedema with ACE inhibitors. Safety-relevant: the app would also triage this as a red flag.

questions.question: Can she take Aleve for her knee pain?
questions.why: NSAID with an ACE inhibitor and a diuretic. Brand name only (Aleve).

questions.question: What is the difference between metoprolol succinate and metoprolol tartrate?
questions.why: The look-alike trap: both labels are in the corpus (tartrate is her stopped medicine).

questions.question: Her old doctor had her on amlodipine. Can it cause swollen ankles?
questions.why: Peripheral edema. Amlodipine is not in Rosa's plan, so it enters the search only because the question names it (metadata filter).

questions.question: What happens if she accidentally takes two of her water pills?
questions.why: Overdose section. The app itself would still send dose questions to the pharmacy [contact-2].

questions.question: What are the side effects of Zorvexa?
questions.why: No answer: Zorvexa is a made-up drug (same name as in the stress suite).

questions.question: Is it okay for her to do some gardening this week after coming home?
questions.why: No answer: activity advice is not in any drug label.
